while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    COUNT=$((COUNT + 1))
    name=$(basename "$ref")

    # A ref that was pushed from here is already local. Resolving it is a read;
    # fetching one that is not would change this repository, so it is reported
    # as unknown instead.
    if ! git rev-parse --quiet --verify "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf '%-52s %10s %7s %7s\n' "$name" "not local" "-" "-"
        continue
    fi

    # Walk the tree rather than the whole archive. A checkpoint holds the
    # session transcript, which runs to megabytes, and putting that through a
    # shell variable is what made an earlier version of this script report
    # zero for every ref.
    bytes=0
    homes=0
    mails=0
    while read -r _mode _type blob size path; do
        case "$size" in ''|*[!0-9]*) continue ;; esac
        bytes=$((bytes + size))
        case "$path" in
            *.jsonl|*.json|*.txt)
                h=$(git cat-file blob "$blob" 2>/dev/null \
                    | { grep -coE '/home/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' || true; })
                m=$(git cat-file blob "$blob" 2>/dev/null \
                    | { grep -coE '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}' || true; })
                homes=$((homes + ${h:-0}))
                mails=$((mails + ${m:-0}))
                ;;
        esac
    done <<TREE
$(git ls-tree -r --long "$ref" 2>/dev/null)
TREE

    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + bytes))
    HOMES=$((HOMES + homes))
    MAILS=$((MAILS + mails))

    printf '%-52s %10s %7s %7s\n' "$name" "$bytes" "$homes" "$mails"
done <<EOF

content.text:
Phase 14 is complete and pushed. Nine commits, `06a9bcf` through `9ce0a95`, `go test ./...` green at each.

## The six render screenshots

`umbra/docs/renders/`, all captured from headless Chrome against `site/index.html`, not from reading the CSS:

| file | scheme | playhead |
|---|---|---|
| `lightfield-dark-seq0.png` | night | seq 0, before the sweep |
| `lightfield-dark-cut.png` | night | at the cut |
| `lightfield-dark-end.png` | night | end of the replay |
| `lightfield-light-seq0.png` | day | seq 0 |
| `lightfield-light-cut.png` | day | at the cut |
| `lightfield-light-end.png` | day | end |

The first-pass image that was sitting at the repository root is now `lightfield-first-pass.png` in the same directory, kept for comparison. Nothing image-shaped remains at the root.

What the browser confirmed rather than what the code says: 10 gradient stops on `(1-t)³`, opacity reaching zero at 85% of the radius so there is no rim in either scheme; radius scaling by `500/n^0.25` when several sources are lit; day-scheme peak 0.15 against night's 0.32, so under half; pools drawn in `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 18%, transparent)`; and 11 of 11 nodes carrying a pool blob keyed by node id, transitioning over 240 ms as the sweep moves. That last one was a real bug: blobs were only being created for nodes that had a pool at render time, so lit nodes could never gain one during replay.

## The two landing maps

**Seeded.** Checkpoint `b20f84567474`, commit `0063443`, from this session. 11 nodes, 4 sources, 2 lit / 3 penumbra / 6 umbra. Coverage: 2 file reads, 4 edits, 47 shell commands. The session-said line is the real fallback the tool printed, with its real origin note: *"what the agent said after its last edit, because Entire stored no summary."* The old map was the authored `classic` scenario, checkpoint `sample000class`, commit all zeros, session `scenario-session`, with a hand-written sentence, under a caption calling it a real report. The caption now says what is arranged is the fixture app, not the session. `TestSampleIsNotScripted` in `internal/report/site_test.go` fails on any of those three markers, and `gen-site` no longer synthesizes a report at all: it reads the committed one and refuses it if it looks written.

**Not seeded.** Checkpoint `9b940c5e4916`, commit `0941dad`, a LockStep session imported with `entire import` and analyzed with `--run none`. 4 nodes, 3 sources, all four dependents umbra. Coverage: 40 file reads, 122 edits, 1156 shell commands, so it is not the shell-only case you told me to keep anyway; the agent read and edited plenty and still never looked at any of the four things its change reached. The clone was made into scratch so LockStep itself got no hooks, settings or commits. Scrubbed with the existing scrubber and the artifacts tests run against it.

That import found a real leak. Only `umbra record` was setting `scrub.Names`, so the analysis path let the author's name through into `timeline[].cmd`. Two occurrences. `gitNames()` moved into `analyze.go`. A related one in 14.1 was worse: `graph.Verify` appended its commands to `a.Commands` raw, bypassing the scrubber that every other command went through, which put an absolute home path into `site/sample/umbra.json`. I committed 14.1 with that test red because my check counted `ok` lines instead of looking for `FAIL`; I amended it, so no commit is left failing, but the commit was wrong when I made it.

## Test count

**298**, from 253 at the start of the phase. New: five label-layout tests across all eight scenarios, the sample-is-real test, a change-kind table test, and the cross-implementation mirror extended to three playhead positions per scenario, now comparing 384 cases.

## The two scripts, neither executed

`scripts/graft.sh --dry-run` prints every command and runs none: fork `entireio/entire-graph` (resolves to `u7k4rs6/entire-graph`), clone to `~/.cache/umbra-graft`, branch `umbra` from `upstream/main`, rsync `umbra/` in, `entire enable --agent claude-code`, then two commits, documents first. It never pushes.

Writing it turned up a documentation problem worth your attention. The instruction was to enable Entire with the India mirror "as documented", and **there is no way to do that from this CLI**. `entire enable`, `entire login` and `entire configure` were all checked against 0.10.5 and none takes a region flag. The India region came from the Impeach handoff, read in the first minutes of this build while I was establishing it was not Umbra's. The script does what the CLI supports, notes that the mirror follows the account you log in as rather than the checkout, and prints who that is.

`scripts/checkpoint-refs-audit.sh` reads only. Before the phase 14 push: 30 refs, 288,677,347 bytes, 48,408 lines with a home path, 420 with an email address. Straight after: **39 refs, 413,032,568 bytes, 71,147 path lines, 708 address lines.** Nine commits added 124 MB and 288 more addressed lines. Largest single ref 15.8 MB; smallest is the phase 12 minimal recording at 27 KB with no addresses at all.

Three bugs came out of running it, and the third is why I would not trust this script unread: `git ls-tree` is scoped to the working directory, and the script runs from `umbra/`, so it first reported thirty refs of zero bytes carrying no paths and no addresses. A confident, precise, completely wrong all-clear on the exact question the script exists to answer. It needs `--full-tree`. The other two were `grep` exiting non-zero under `pipefail`, and buffering a 10 MB archive into a shell variable.

## The Concepts images

I said I would put a proposal to you rather than quietly overrule FRONTEND_SPEC. What I can take without breaking it: the legend as pills rather than a paragraph, a serif display face for the two headings against the mono body, mono micro-labels under each map, and a warmer accent than the current one. What I cannot: the photographic hero, which needs an image request, and the spec forbids requests and fonts. That is a change to `site/index.html` and `umbra.css` only, no report changes, maybe an hour. Say the word and it is a separate commit.
